summary: The round 1 fixes land cleanly. The decline-reopen exception, the per-pass why_human schema, the findings file's `scoped` key, the review-body overrule door, the scope-declined thread reason and the two refactors all do what their findings asked. Only the R1-13 move introduced a defect: checkWhy now runs after checkSpec, so a refused reason's stage error names the spec-status call instead of the shaper. Beyond that, the coverage pass found places where the new model's bookkeeping does not match what it posts. A free-text ref mints a duplicate finding. A deferred or declined item counts as fixed in the final nit pass wording. A decline the person accepts is listed as overruled. A reshape can stop a call from buying a round. The repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs (no routes/console.php), so there is no overlap to report.

findings.title: prior-findings' login patterns reject a login with an underscore
findings.description: This pull request names the person by login in the rule reply (`left to @<login> under repository rule <id>`) and in the review-body tail (` · left to @<login> under rule <id>`). The two patterns that read them back allow only `@[A-Za-z0-9-]+` (classify at line 358, the title capture at line 365). Reproduced with jq. `"left to @octo_acme under repository rule x (y)" | test(...)` returns false, so the reply falls through to `decided` instead of `left`. The capture on `"Title · left to @octo_acme under rule x"` returns the whole tail as the title. The next run's reviewer prompt (handled list) and the handoff's Earlier rounds would then show the polluted title. Condition: the login contains `_`. GitHub Enterprise Managed User logins are `<handle>_<shortcode>`; that is a GitHub fact, not something this repository shows. `redline-setup.sh:796` also rejects `_` in `--reviewer`, outside this diff. Both `left` and `decided` are tracked dispositions, so the finding is not re-raised.
findings.proposedFix: Widen both alternatives to `@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` (lines 358 and 365) and add a gh-test fixture row with an underscore login.

findings.title: KINDS tells the final nit pass that a correctness finding buys another round
findings.description: `reviewPrompt` pushes KINDS into every review prompt, the final nit pass included (line 1389). KINDS ends 'a correctness finding the run acts on buys another round' (line 346). In a final nit pass, a correctness finding gets one more revise pass and then the run ends (lines 3817-3830, and 3696-3705 after a human pass), so in that prompt the sentence is false. The candidate also says the final-nit-pass prompt says the run stops after one more pass. It does not: line 1385 states only the scope. R1-8 fixed the same kind of clash for FACTS_ONLY; KINDS was left as it was.
findings.proposedFix: Leave out the last sentence of KINDS on a final nit pass, or add a clause there such as 'in a final nit pass it buys one more revise pass and then the run ends', and pin it in the loop test.

findings.title: Per-pass shaper schema splits why_human but not the disposition enum
findings.description: The R1-5/R1-12 fix builds `shapeSchema(reasons)` per pass, so a value from the other pass is refused in the shaper's own run (comment at lines 672-674). Only `why_human` differs. Both schemas keep `disposition` as ['fix','decline','defer','ask','none'] (line 692). A human pass's shaper can therefore return `decline` or `defer`, and a Redline round's shaper can return `none`. Each passes structured output and then stops the run at shape in checkDispositions (lines 2563-2584). A resume reruns the same prompt. humanShapePrompt (line 1663) says 'Sort each finding into fix, ask or none; never defer' and the agent file's rule 8 says never decline, so this needs the shaper to ignore both.
findings.proposedFix: Pass the disposition enum into shapeSchema too: ['fix','ask','none'] for SHAPE_SCHEMAS.human and ['fix','decline','defer','ask'] for SHAPE_SCHEMAS.round. Keep checkDispositions as the second layer, and add a loop check on the `shape h1` schema's disposition enum.

findings.title: The pass's person label is recomputed by a ternary at five sites
findings.description: The human-pass label is recomputed inline at five sites: line 1130 (`human ? 'The author' : personLabel`), 1160 and 2512 (`human ? 'the person' : personLabel`), 1296 and 2545 (`human ? 'the author' : personLabel`). The candidate says about seven; it is five. Two of them use 'the person' rather than 'the author', so one field would need two words or one wording would change. No wrong output today: droppedReplies calls describeOutcome without `human` (lines 2746, 2748), but the `dropped` kind does not read it.
findings.proposedFix: Put the label on passOf (for example `pass.person` and `pass.Person`) and read it at those sites, keeping the human pass's 'the person' wording where it differs, or record why the two words stay separate.

findings.title: A verified or unconfirmed ref with text after the id mints a duplicate correctness finding
findings.description: For a `verified` or `unconfirmed` entry, accountCoverage looks up `byId.get(ref)` with the whole trimmed ref (lines 1535-1537). A ref such as 'R1-1 (the guard)' misses, a warning is pushed, and the index is added to `told` (lines 1538-1541). The fill loop then mints a new finding for that index: correctness, medium, unconfirmed, with the candidate's claim, which repeats R1-1 (lines 1562-1571). It is posted inline, shaped on its own, and as a correctness finding it can buy a round or, past the cap, appear in the cap-hit comment. The ref field is a free string in the schema. The prompt asks for the id alone, so this needs the verifier to add text after it. The `duplicate` branch already reads past such text with a leading-token parse (line 2363), and agents.md:30 asks that a parsed field read past it. On main the same slip produced only a For the person line (base accountCoverage).
findings.proposedFix: Read the leading id token for these outcomes, e.g. `const id = (/^(R\d+-\d+)\b/.exec(ref) || [])[1] || ref; const finding = byId.get(id)`, keep the warning when text follows the id, and add a loop check where 'R1-1 (note)' counts as R1-1 and mints nothing.

findings.title: A minted finding from a candidate with no file posts a line prior-findings cannot read back
findings.description: The candidate parser defaults a missing file to '' and line to 0 (lines 1476-1477). An unaccounted candidate is now minted as a finding with that file and line (line 1567). findingLine then writes ``- **R2-n** · correctness · medium · unconfirmed · `:0` · ...`` (line 908). prior-findings' finding_lines needs `` `(?<file>[^`]+):(?<line>[0-9]+)` `` (redline-gh.sh:343), and `:0` has no character before the colon, so the line is skipped. A later run neither carries the finding nor sees it as settled, and its reply has nothing to attach to. This needs the skill to return a candidate with no file and the verifier to leave it out. On main such a candidate went to For the person, which was not read back either, but this pull request makes it a finding with an id and a thread.
findings.proposedFix: When minting from a candidate with no file, use a placeholder the reader accepts (for example the PR's first changed file, or a fixed `(no file)` with line 0, and widen finding_lines to allow it), or make the body line carry a marker prior-findings reads. Add a loop check and a gh fixture row.

findings.title: relaunch.how still gives a decisions hand-off's decisions without `disposition`
findings.description: result().relaunch.how says a decisions hand-off relaunches with decisions `{"<id>": {"choice", "notes", "date"}}` (line 2220). This pull request lets a typed line at that stop overrule a decline, recorded with `disposition` (skills/redline/SKILL.md:208). overridesFor applies a decision only when it has `disposition` (line 2888). A session that relaunches from relaunch.how, not the skill, would record the overrule without it. The decline would then be posted as declined although the person overruled it. The line is unchanged from main (it sits outside this pull request's diff); the overrule that makes it stale is this pull request's. The skill, the documented driver, records `disposition`.
findings.proposedFix: Change the decisions hand-off clause to `decisions ({"<id>": {"choice", "notes", "date"}}, every decision so far, unchanged, plus `"disposition": "fix|defer"` on an overruled decline)`.

findings.title: checkCalls takes a `pass` parameter it no longer reads
findings.description: After R1-13 moved the why_human test into checkWhy, checkCalls (lines 2603-2618) reads only `shaped` and `known`. `pass` is unused. Both call sites (lines 2847 and 2965) still pass it, which suggests the check depends on the pass kind when it does not.
findings.proposedFix: Drop the `pass` parameter from checkCalls and its two call sites.

findings.title: checkWhy's stage error names the spec-status label, so a resume replays the refused shaper
findings.description: stageError takes `lastLabel` when no label is given (lines 460-463), and run() sets it to each agent's label (line 499). checkWhy now runs after checkSpec (lines 2848-2850; 2966-2968 on a reshape). checkSpec's run sets lastLabel to `spec status r<n>` (or `spec status r<n> #N`). The throw at line 2630 therefore carries that label, and resumeFrom names the spec-status call, not `shape r<n>`. The other shaper checks name the shaper. On resume the shaper's prompt is unchanged, so its refused output replays from cache, only the read-only spec check reruns, and checkWhy throws the same error again. Before the R1-13 fix the test sat in checkCalls, ahead of checkSpec, and named `shape r<n>`. Condition: checkWhy fires only when a why_human outside the round's enum reaches the workflow. The per-pass schema now refuses that value in the shaper's own run, and round 1's set-aside refutation says the structured-output tool validates enums. So this needs a schema leak.
findings.proposedFix: Pass the shaper's label to the error: give checkWhy a `shaperLabel` argument (`shape ${pass.tag}`, or `reshape ${pass.tag} #N`) and throw `stageError('shape', ..., {}, shaperLabel)`. Add a loop check that the resumeFrom label is the shaper's.

findings.title: A plan-dial 'accept' of a shaper decline is listed as overruled
findings.description: `overruled` is true for any `decided` outcome whose finding was not a judgment call (line 3102). On the plan dial the skill offers changing a decline to `accept` and calls only a change to fix or defer an overrule (skills/redline/SKILL.md:183). Trace: the shaper declines R1-2, and the person records {disposition: 'accept', notes: 'Agreed, leave it.'}. overridesFor picks it up (line 2888). outcomesFor gives `decided` because a decision exists (lines 2513-2514). overruled is true because R1-2 is no call. The handoff then lists R1-2 under `### Overruled by @login` (line 3228), counts it in the Rounds line as 'overruled by' (line 3207), and drops it from Declined by Redline. The skill's closing summary reports it as overruled (`overruled` true).
findings.proposedFix: Exclude an `accept` that confirms a decline, e.g. `overruled: kind === 'decided' && !calls.some(...) && !(shaperDisposition === 'decline' && decision.disposition === 'accept')`. Either report it as declined with the person's agreement or give it its own group. Add a loop check.

findings.title: `bought` misses a correctness item put to the person when a reshape re-sorts it to decline
findings.description: `bought` reads only the last shaper JSON (`shaperOwn`, line 3125) and the effective dispositions (`finalOwn`, line 3126). Trace: the first shape returns correctness R1-2 as `ask`, and the person answers 'Keep it'. The decision carries no `disposition`, so effectiveDispositions leaves the shaper's value (lines 2930-2933). The plan bounces and the reshape returns R1-2 as `decline` with a reason. checkCalls skips R1-2 because its call is in `calls` (lines 2609-2611), and no check refuses the re-sort. Both maps now read `decline`, so `bought` is false. The run then ends, or goes to a final nit pass, against the done rule that an item put to the person buys the next round. Condition: the reshape must change a decided finding's disposition despite reshapePrompt's 'Decisions already recorded as decided in shape.md stay as they are' (line 1686).
findings.proposedFix: Count a call as buying: `inScope.some((f) => f.category === 'correctness' && (calls.some((c) => c.id === f.id) || ['fix','defer','ask'].includes(shaperOwn[f.id]) || ['fix','defer'].includes(finalOwn[f.id])))`. Optionally have checkCalls warn when a reshape changes a decided call's finding. Add a loop check.

findings.title: `fixed` counts a deferred item's mitigation and any commit naming a declined item
findings.description: `fixed` is every in-scope item whose outcome has a commit (line 3128). outcomesFor sets `commits: named` for a deferred item (its mitigation commit, line 2516) and for a declined one (any commit whose message mentions the id, line 2519). In a final nit pass `final.fixed` comes from this list (line 3828). Trace for a defer: the shaper defers the nit pass's one correctness item R2-1 with a mitigation commit. final.fixed === final.found, so the handoff opens 'The final nit pass found a correctness bug in the nit fixes; it was fixed in one more pass' (line 3156) and sets lastFixUnreviewed (line 3830), while the same comment lists R2-1 under Deferred with the full fix open. The human pass's summary uses the same count (lines 3701, 3332-3336). For a decline, a commit message must mention the declined id. The comment at lines 3148-3149 and this pull request's description promise that no wording calls a declined item fixed.
findings.proposedFix: Count only fixed and applied outcomes: `inScope.filter((f) => ['fixed','decided'].includes(outcomes[f.id].kind) && outcomes[f.id].commits.length > 0)`. Keep a deferral's mitigation in the main loop's `fixedAny` if the done rule wants it to buy the recheck, and let the final-nit-pass wording name deferred items apart. Add loop checks for a deferred and a declined item in a final nit pass.

findings.title: handoffComment writes each outcome group's test twice
findings.description: The tests that sort decidedAll into groups are written once for the lists (asked, auto, overruled, declined, notPicked, notChanged, fixed; lines 3189-3195). They are written again inside the Rounds table's `count(...)` calls (lines 3202-3210). Changing one grouping (as R2-10 would for `overruled`) needs both edits. If they drift, the Rounds counts stop matching the lists below them.
findings.proposedFix: Define one table of {test, label} and drive both the per-round counts and the lists from it.

findings.title: The Fixed list's caption says 'Each in its own commit', which is not always so
findings.description: The folded Fixed list's summary is 'Each in its own commit' (line 3254, new in this pull request). describeOutcome lists every commit that names a fixed item (line 2537), so one item can have two commits and two items can share one. This pull request's own round 1 shows both: R1-12 and R1-5 share c5a2d90, and R1-5 is 'fixed in c5a2d90 and d7b1b65'.
findings.proposedFix: Caption it with what the lines show, e.g. 'With the commits that fixed each'.

findings.title: A second decisions stop lists a decline again that the person already overruled
findings.description: handoffResult builds `declined` from the shaper's raw dispositions (line 3627) and ignores args.decisions. Trace: on guided, the person overrules R1-3 at the first stop and relaunches. The shaper replays from cache with R1-3 still `decline`. The resolve agent returns `unresolved` for a call (line 2917, which hands back the same `shaped`), so the round stops again. handoffResult lists R1-3 under `declined`, and the skill presents it as a decline that 'is posted with its reason' if nobody overrules it (SKILL.md:208). The overrule is still in args.decisions and is applied on the next relaunch, so only what the person is shown is wrong.
findings.proposedFix: Leave out of `declined` any id whose decision in `decisions` carries a disposition, or mark it as already overruled.
